title: Normalization of the explicit absorbing-wall Macdonald noncolliding-walk kernel for real q and t between zero and one
author: Leonid Petrov
source_title: Noncolliding Macdonald Walks with an Absorbing Wall
difficulty_reason: The proof encodes a fixed particle configuration as defects in growing partitions and evaluates the principal-specialized branching kernel in that encoding. It separately controls and cancels all large-size powers, coarm/coleg factors, hook products and dual Pieri factors, leaving the specified finite-particle kernel. These asymptotic and telescoping computations establish its normalization from a prior branching rule rather than simply defining a stochastic kernel by renormalization.
source_version: Official SIGMA 18 (2022) article 079, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2022.079; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Complete author Theorem1.1 proof in Sections3.1–3.7, including full new hook-ratio Proposition3.2, is supplied. Fix m>=1 and real0<q,t<1; x1>...>xm>=0 and y is in the same ordered chamber with yi-xi in{-1,0}. The exact kernel is formula1.3, with its (t,q)-Vandermonde definition1.1 and no change of q/t ordering. The maps pi and pi-bar encode fixed particle defects in finite partitions, and all terms in the large-N principal specialization are explicitly evaluated in the source. Prior Macdonald branching/principal-specialization/dual-hook identities are author-identified background; the new limiting kernel and cancellations are fully written. Eventual absorption, Gibbs tiling weights and Jack/Hall–Littlewood scaling variants are not separately counted.
